- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–3% for 2–4 days post-sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates true volatility in low-sentiment periods; increase forecast variance by 10–20% if sentiment is negative for 5+ consecutive days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion after 3–5 consecutive high values; apply downward correction of 1–4% per day if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often overfits to recent momentum; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to overfit to recent highs; use 3-day moving average of true values as baseline for correction.
